items.answer: Extended Reality (XR) is an umbrella term, not a specific technology, that covers all present or future immersive technologies, such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and mixed reality (MR).
Augmented reality on the reality-virtuality continuum is the intermediate state in which the real environment is augmented with virtual content.

Mixed reality, in a broad sense, is the entire space between the real environment extreme and the virtual environment extreme of the reality-virtuality continuum, containing different degrees of augmentation of the real environment with virtual content and of the virtual environment with real content.

Extended Reality (XR) is an umbrella term, not a specific technology, that covers all present or future immersive technologies, such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and mixed reality (MR).

An immersive experience is a perceived experience through sensory organs that appears real: when a person experiences an environment through sensory organs and fails to distinguish that environment from the person's real environment, perceiving it as the real environment, the technology producing that experience is an immersive technology.

questions.question: Why can a relatively small share of XR applications in defense still be commercially important?
options: Defense is expected to have the largest percentage share of XR applications.
Worldwide military budgets are large, so even a small percentage can represent a large monetary amount.
Defense is commercially promising because its application share is expected to shrink.
Defense is commercially promising because it uses only headsets, making it cheaper.
questions.explanation: The segment says that, because worldwide military budgets are huge, even a small percentage of defense applications can be a large monetary amount, so commercial penetration can be expected.

questions.question: Why are VR or MR particularly useful in medical education and training?
options: They let patients visit faraway hospitals without traveling or physical effort.
They let buyers inspect upcoming properties before spending large amounts.
They let trainees explore body organs, their appearance, function, and parts even when cadavers are difficult to obtain.
They let soldiers practice combat training with wireless weapon controllers.
questions.explanation: Healthcare is a prominent VR/MR domain for medical education and training, where immersive simulations help potential doctors learn about organs and are useful when obtaining cadavers is difficult.

questions.question: What is a main benefit of using immersive technologies in education for an appropriate duration?
options: They can improve learner engagement and learning outcomes compared with standard teaching methods.
They are most beneficial when used for excessive durations.
They replace standard teaching methods without changing learning outcomes.
They are beneficial only at the tertiary education level.
questions.explanation: Appropriate exposure to immersive technologies in education can improve engagement and learning outcomes compared with standard methods, although excessive duration may create problems.

questions.question: Why is digital heritage preservation a suitable application for immersive technologies?
options: It lets large numbers of users physically enter restricted areas of the site.
It stops physical decay by making the entire heritage site fully virtual.
It requires every part of the heritage site to be physically accessible to visitors.
It allows users to explore heritage spaces that cannot be physically visited by large numbers, while preserving parts digitally.
questions.explanation: Digital heritage preservation is suitable because heritage places may not be physically visited by large numbers or in all parts, and immersive technologies can preserve the space digitally despite physical decay.

data.text: Extended reality has commercial potential in various sectors, and penetration in the commercial space can be expected both percentage-wise and value-wise. Gaming, healthcare, and education are prominent or emerging domains that use immersive technologies to improve popularity, training, and engagement, although excessive duration may create problems. The automobile, travel, tourism, and digital heritage sectors are evolving or emerging areas that use immersive experiences for virtual exploration. Finally, real estate and architecture allow for the exploration of properties, while defense provides simulations for specialized military training.
points: Extended reality has commercial potential in various sectors, and penetration in the commercial space can be expected both percentage-wise and value-wise.
Gaming and entertainment is a current VR domain that uses immersive technologies to make gaming more acceptable and popular.
Healthcare is a prominent domain for training, and education is an emerging domain that can improve engagement and outcomes, although excessive duration may create problems.
The automobile, travel, tourism, and digital heritage sectors are evolving or emerging areas that use immersive technologies for virtual exploration.
Real estate and architecture allow for exploring properties, while defense is a major area for simulations used in specialized military training.

questions.question: In virtual reality, what does immersion require of the user's sensory input?
options: The user's senses are blocked so input comes only from the virtual world.
The user's eyes are blocked while ears and skin remain exposed to real signals.
The user is psychologically engaged while physically attached to the real world.
The user's eyes, ears, and other sensory organs remain open to the real world.
questions.explanation: Immersion in VR means the user's senses are blocked so that no input comes from the real-world environment, and input comes only from the virtual world.

questions.question: Why are VR systems categorized as non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive?
options: The price of the hardware alone determines the sensory blocking level.
Commercial VR systems must block all senses to be fully immersive.
Market applications offer different degrees of immersion rather than all being fully immersive.
Each category is defined by a different real-world application domain.
questions.explanation: VR systems are categorized this way because market applications provide varying degrees of immersion instead of all being fully immersive.

questions.question: How does a non-immersive VR application affect the user?
options: It blocks all senses, making the user feel physically present in the virtual world.
It blocks the eyes while leaving ears and skin exposed to the real world.
It captures attention, but sensory organs remain open and the user stays physically attached to the real world.
It uses gloves, body connectors, and body suits to detect physical movements.
questions.explanation: A non-immersive VR application can completely take the user's attention, but the eyes, ears, and other sensory organs remain open and the user remains physically attached to the real world.

questions.question: A three-dimensional virtual tour that is experienced through a headset with no real physical movement is an example of which VR system type?
options: Non-immersive VR
Semi-immersive VR
Augmented reality
Fully immersive VR
questions.explanation: Semi-immersive VR can be a three-dimensional virtual environment experienced through a VR headset, with examples including virtual tours using only a headset, while users typically have no real physical movements.

data.text: Immersion in virtual reality means that the user's senses are blocked from the real-world environment so they receive input only from the virtual world. Systems are categorized into non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive based on the degree of sensory blocking. Non-immersive and semi-immersive systems are common and cost-effective, while fully immersive systems are the costliest and rarest because they completely block all senses.
points: Immersion in VR means the user's senses are blocked from the real world so they only receive input from the virtual world.
VR systems are categorized into non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive systems based on the degree of sensory blocking.
Non-immersive systems allow users to control virtual activities while remaining physically attached to the real world.
Semi-immersive systems provide partial immersion by blocking some senses while leaving the user free to sense the real world.
Fully immersive systems completely block all senses but are the costliest and rarest systems.

questions.question: Why can an immersive experience that is perceived as real be useful in both healthcare and travel and tourism?
questions.reference_answer: An immersive experience appears real because the user perceives it as the real environment. In healthcare, virtual reality and mixed reality simulations let potential doctors explore body organs, see their parts, and learn when cadavers are difficult to obtain. In travel and tourism, virtual tours let users visit faraway places without physically going there, saving money and physical effort.

questions.question: Why are most commercial immersive applications semi-immersive rather than fully immersive?
questions.reference_answer: A semi-immersive virtual reality system gives a partial immersive experience by blocking some but not all senses. It is the most cost-effective and commonly used form of virtual reality, so most commercial immersive applications are semi-immersive. A fully immersive virtual reality system is the costliest and commercially rare because it is difficult to afford.

questions.question: How does a non-immersive virtual reality system differ from a semi-immersive virtual reality system in the user's sensory connection to the real world?
questions.reference_answer: A non-immersive virtual reality system is a specific, limited class of computer application in which the user controls characters or activities while retaining control of the physical environment, and the virtual environment does not directly interact with the user. The user may be psychologically engaged while the eyes, ears, and other sensory organs remain open, so the user remains physically attached to the real world. A semi-immersive virtual reality system instead blocks some but not all senses, for example the eyes, while other senses remain exposed to real-world signals.

questions.question: Why do virtual boot camp and combat training systems use motion trackers, full-body tracking systems, and wireless weapon controllers in addition to head-mounted displays?
questions.reference_answer: Defense training includes virtual boot camp and combat training that simulate vehicles, soldiers, and combat environments with constraints. Such training uses head-mounted displays with motion trackers, full-body tracking systems, and wireless weapon controllers. Fully immersive virtual reality systems detect actual movements, reactions, and even a blink of an eye and translate them into actions in the virtual world.
